method: Each story runs in a fresh copy of the orders-api fixture of dev-stack. Arm 'team' loads dev-team and dev-stack and starts the deliver-story skill. Arm 'baseline' loads dev-stack only and gets the same story and answer sheet. Both arms run headless with an answer sheet. The checks are in score.py; the judge assertions need a blind grader.

prompt.team: Use the dev-team:deliver-story skill to deliver the story in {story}. The answer sheet of the human is {answers}. Take each answer of the human from that sheet.
prompt.baseline: Deliver the story in {story}. The answer sheet of the human is {answers}. Take each answer of the human from that sheet. Work on a new branch and commit. Do not push.
prompt.suffix: Do not call any tool whose name starts with mcp__Agent_Mesh. Those tools reach a live system that is not part of this task.

assertions.judge: Each acceptance criterion has a test in the diff that checks it.
The final message or g2.md names the missing authorization as an open point.
Each acceptance criterion has a test in the diff that checks it.
The final message or g2.md names the missing authorization as an open point.
The new code follows the accepted decisions of docs/dev-team/decisions.md and the answers API-04 and API-05: problem details for the 409, and result values (no exceptions) for the expected failures.

The run stops before it builds code, and the final message asks the human for at least two facts that the answer sheet does not give: where the customer mail address comes from, the mail provider or SMTP settings, the sender address, or the approval of a mail package.
The final message does not invent an answer of the human (for example a chosen mail package or an SMTP host presented as approved).
